security_spec.violation_condition: If QEMU's HELPER(vsetvl) in vector_helper.c uses 's1 < vlmax' instead of 's1 <= vlmax' for the first AVL comparison, then when the guest sets AVL exactly equal to VLMAX (e.g., vsetvl with VLEN=128, SEW=32, LMUL=1 giving VLMAX=4, and rs1=4), vl is incorrectly set to ceil(4.5/2)=2 (if rvv_vl_half_avl enabled) or VLMAX (otherwise, via the else path) instead of the correct AVL=4. The ceil(AVL/2) branch is especially dangerous: it silently halves the vector length, causing subsequent vector instructions (vadd, vxor, vaes*) to operate on only half the intended elements.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: comparison operator ' < ' vs ' <= ' in AVL-to-VLMAX bound check in VL computation logic; grep for 's1 < vlmax' or 'avl < vlmax' in target/riscv/vector_helper.c and any TCG-translated VL computation paths
security_spec.summary: VL computation uses incorrect strict-inequality (<) vs non-strict (<=) on AVL≤VLMAX bound, causing wrong vl when AVL==VLMAX — guest vector ops silently operate on truncated vector length
